title: Hire the One Staff Member Who Works While You Are Asleep
author: How to Teach With AI
source: How to Teach With AI (howtoteachwithai.substack.com), August 17, 2026
summary: This installment of a teacher-focused AI workflow series walks readers through setting up Claude Code as an automated 'Senior Analyst' that stress-tests lesson plans overnight against four struggling-student personas (bored, confused, overwhelmed, checked-out) and produces a rebuilt plan by morning. The piece frames the tool choice as a matter of delegation leash length rather than raw intelligence: conversational AI tools like Cowork require the teacher present, while Claude Code runs a defined multi-step workflow unattended. It gives a literal four-step setup (open the Code tab, point it at a lesson-plans folder, drop in a custom Skill file, type one instruction) that the author claims takes 30 minutes once and five minutes every week thereafter. The piece is explicitly aimed at the K-12 teacher's Sunday-night lesson-prep bottleneck, contrasting a future where teachers manually and incompletely stress-test plans against one where an agent runs the full battery of checks while they sleep. It closes with a specific SKILL.md template teachers can copy directly into their own folder structure.
points: Distinguishes Cowork-style conversational AI assistance from Claude Code's unattended agentic workflow using a 'how much leash you give it' framing, arguing the difference that matters is autonomy, not underlying model intelligence.

Supplies a copy-pasteable Skill template that runs four named student personas (bored, confused, overwhelmed, checked-out) against a lesson plan and outputs a rebuilt version plus per-persona failure reports.
Targets the specific Sunday-night teacher bottleneck of manually running mental stress tests on lesson plans, arguing manual effort collapses in quality by the second or third plan due to fatigue.
Frames the tool's value in a Monday-morning-after comparison: catching failure points before class Tuesday versus discovering them live when a bored student pulls out their phone.
Positions total setup cost at 30 minutes once, five minutes per week thereafter, explicitly to lower the activation barrier for teachers hesitant about agentic AI tools.
quotes: You told yourself you'd run five student personas through each plan. You ran two. You called it good. You went to bed. That job was never yours. That was a Senior Analyst job.

You tell Cowork 'grade this one submission' and talk with it. You tell Code 'run the 4-persona stress test on every lesson plan in the Week9 folder' and close your laptop. The difference is not intelligence. The difference is how much leash you give it.
Total first-time setup is 30 minutes. Every Sunday after that is five minutes.
Be specific. Point to lines in the plan. Do not write generic advice about engagement. Do not soften. If a spot is going to kill the lesson, say so.
In the other, Claude Code ran all four personas against all three plans while you were asleep. You woke up Monday. You read the reports over coffee. You rebuilt the one plan that had three red flags.
